This document outlines the envisioned file structure and core responsibilities for the ARTTOO Design Studio, assuming all advanced features (text controls, element manipulation, drawing tools, layers, effects, undo/redo, etc.) are fully implemented in a modular, production-ready manner.

I. Core State Management (src/stores/designStore.ts) This Zustand store will be the single source of truth for the Design Studio's canvas state.

// src/stores/designStore.ts import { create } from 'zustand'; import { type TextElement, type ShapeElement, type ImageElement, type ProcessedImageElement, // Potentially: type DrawnPathElement, type GroupElement } from '@/types/design-elements'; // Assuming all element types are here

type DesignElement = TextElement | ShapeElement | ImageElement | ProcessedImageElement /* | DrawnPathElement | GroupElement */;

interface HistoryState { past: DesignState[]; present: DesignState; future: DesignState[]; }

interface DesignState { elements: DesignElement[]; selectedElementIds: string[]; activeTool: string; currentElementSubTool: string | null; // e.g., 'rectangle', 'ellipse' for 'Elements' tool toolSettings: { // Example: For Draw tool drawBrushType: string; drawBrushSize: number; drawBrushColor: string; drawOpacity: number; // Example: For Text tool (defaults before element creation) defaultFontFamily: string; defaultFontSize: number; defaultFontColor: string; // ... other tool-specific settings }; canvasZoom: number; canvasPan: { x: number; y: number }; gridSettings: { visible: boolean; size: number; snapToGrid: boolean; }; baseImage: string | null; // The main background image for the canvas // Potentially: canvasWidth, canvasHeight if dynamic }

interface DesignStore extends DesignState { history: HistoryState; // Manages undo/redo for the DesignState properties // --- Actions --- // Element Actions addElement: (element: DesignElement) => void; removeElements: (elementIds: string[]) => void; updateElement: (elementId: string, updates: Partial<DesignElement>) => void; updateMultipleElements: (updates: Array<{ id: string; props: Partial<DesignElement> }>) => void; setSelectedElementIds: (ids: string[]) => void; clearSelection: () => void; bringToFront: (elementIds: string[]) => void; // Reorders in the elements array or updates zIndex sendToBack: (elementIds: string[]) => void; duplicateElements: (elementIds: string[]) => void; groupElements: (elementIds: string[]) => void; // Creates a GroupElement ungroupElement: (groupId: string) => void;

// Tool Actions setActiveTool: (tool: string, subTool?: string | null) => void; updateToolSetting: (tool: string, setting: string, value: any) => void;

// Canvas Actions setCanvasZoom: (zoom: number) => void; setCanvasPan: (pan: { x: number; y: number }) => void; setGridVisibility: (visible: boolean) => void; setBaseImage: (imageUri: string | null) => void; clearCanvas: () => void; // Resets elements, baseImage, selections

// History Actions undo: () => void; redo: () => void; takeSnapshot: () => void; // Called after significant actions }

export const useDesignStore = create<DesignStore>((set, get) => ({ // --- Initial State --- elements: [], selectedElementIds: [], activeTool: 'Select', currentElementSubTool: null, toolSettings: { drawBrushType: 'pen', drawBrushSize: 5, drawBrushColor: '#000000', drawOpacity: 1, defaultFontFamily: 'system-ui, sans-serif', defaultFontSize: 16, defaultFontColor: '#000000', }, canvasZoom: 1, canvasPan: { x: 0, y: 0 }, gridSettings: { visible: false, size: 20, snapToGrid: false }, baseImage: null, history: { past: [], present: { /* initial serializable state for undo/redo */ } as DesignState, // Will be populated by initial snapshot future: [], },

// --- Action Implementations (examples) --- addElement: (element) => { set((state) => ({ elements: [...state.elements, element] })); get().takeSnapshot(); }, updateElement: (elementId, updates) => { set((state) => ({ elements: state.elements.map(el => el.id === elementId ? { ...el, ...updates } : el), })); // Note: takeSnapshot might be called by the UI action that triggers updateElement // or could be debounced here for continuous updates like dragging. }, setSelectedElementIds: (ids) => set({ selectedElementIds: ids }), setActiveTool: (tool, subTool = null) => set({ activeTool: tool, currentElementSubTool: subTool, selectedElementIds: [] }), // Deselect on tool change clearCanvas: () => { set({ elements: [], selectedElementIds: [], baseImage: null, // Reset other relevant states if needed }); get().takeSnapshot(); }, takeSnapshot: () => { // Logic to capture serializable parts of the current state // and update history.past, history.present // This needs careful implementation to avoid storing non-serializable data // or excessively large states. }, undo: () => { /* Logic to revert to past state / }, redo: () => { / Logic to advance to future state */ }, // ... other action implementations }));

II. Main Design Studio Page (src/app/design-studio/page.tsx) This file orchestrates the overall layout and connects UI interactions to the designStore.

Responsibilities:

Sets up the main layout using LeftNav, TopBar, VerticalToolbar, DesignCanvasWrapper (new), and RightProperties.

Subscribes to useDesignStore to get data needed for RightProperties and VerticalToolbar (e.g., activeTool, selectedElementIds to determine which properties panel to show).

Provides callbacks to VerticalToolbar and RightProperties that dispatch actions to useDesignStore (e.g., setActiveTool, updateElement for property changes).

Does NOT contain direct canvas rendering logic or complex element state management.

III. Canvas Wrapper (src/components/design-studio/canvas/DesignCanvasWrapper.tsx) (NEW) This component is responsible for the main interactive canvas area.

Responsibilities:

Subscribes to useDesignStore to get elements, canvasZoom, canvasPan, gridSettings, baseImage, activeTool, selectedElementIds.

Manages the rendering loop for canvas elements if using a library like Konva.js or a custom <canvas> solution for drawing/effects. If using HTML elements for text/shapes/images, it maps over them.

Renders the baseImage.

Renders grid lines if gridSettings.visible is true.

Iterates through the elements array from the store and renders each using appropriate display components (e.g., <TextElementDisplay>, <ShapeElementDisplay>).

Handles canvas-level interactions:

Zoom and Pan: Listens for mouse wheel/trackpad gestures for zoom, and mouse drag (e.g., with spacebar pressed) for pan, updating canvasZoom and canvasPan in the store.

Selection:

Click detection on elements (delegated to individual element display components, which then call a store action).

Marquee/rubber-band selection for multiple elements.

Element Creation: Handles clicks on the canvas when a creation tool (Text, Elements, Draw) is active, dispatching actions to useDesignStore.addElement() with initial properties based on click position and toolSettings.

Drawing: If activeTool === 'Draw', it manages a dedicated drawing layer (likely a separate <canvas>) and captures mouse events to create DrawnPathElements.

IV. Element Display Components (src/components/design-studio/elements/) Each component is responsible for rendering a specific type of design element and its interactive handles (selection, resize, rotate).

TextElementDisplay.tsx:

Receives element: TextElement, isSelected: boolean, zoomLevel: number.

Renders text using element.fontFamily, fontSize, color, fontWeight, fontStyle, textAlign, letterSpacing, lineHeight, rotation, textShadow, etc.

Displays selection outline and transformation handles (resize, rotate) when isSelected.

Handles onMouseDown for drag initiation, onClick for selection, and potentially onDoubleClick for on-canvas text editing (which would show an overlayed input).

All interactions dispatch actions to useDesignStore.

ShapeElementDisplay.tsx:

Receives element: ShapeElement (which includes type: 'rectangle' | 'ellipse' | 'polygon' | 'line' | 'star'), isSelected: boolean, zoomLevel: number.

Renders the shape using fillColor (solid/gradient), strokeColor, strokeWidth, strokeStyle, cornerRadius, rotation, opacity, shadowEffect.

Displays selection outline and transformation handles.

Handles interactions and dispatches actions.

ImageElementDisplay.tsx:

Receives element: ImageElement | ProcessedImageElement, isSelected: boolean, zoomLevel: number.

Renders the image, applying opacity, blendMode, filters (brightness, contrast, blur, etc.), rotation.

Displays selection outline and transformation handles.

Handles interactions and dispatches actions.

DrawnPathElementDisplay.tsx (NEW):

Receives element: DrawnPathElement (containing path data d, strokeColor, strokeWidth, strokeOpacity, brushType).

Renders the drawn path (likely as SVG <path> or drawn onto a canvas layer).

Displays selection outline (bounding box of the path).

Handles interactions.

GroupElementDisplay.tsx (NEW):

Receives element: GroupElement (containing childElementIds).

Renders a bounding box encompassing all child elements.

Applies transformations (drag, resize, rotate) to the group, which then propagate to child elements (logic handled in the store or transformation utils).

Displays selection outline and transformation handles for the group.

V. Tool Options Panels (src/components/design-studio/tools/) These components reside within the RightProperties panel and display contextual options based on the activeTool or selectedElementIds from useDesignStore.

TextToolOptions.tsx:

Visible when activeTool === 'Text' (for default settings before creation) OR when a text element is selected.

Controls for: Font Family (selector with web-safe and Google Fonts), Font Weight/Style (bold, italic, underline), Font Size, Text Color, Alignment, Letter Spacing, Line Height, Text Shadow, Opacity.

Dispatch updateElement or updateToolSetting actions.

ShapeToolOptions.tsx:

Visible when a shape element is selected.

Controls for: Fill (color picker, gradient editor), Stroke (color, width, style: solid/dashed/dotted), Corner Radius (for rectangles/polygons), Opacity, Shadow Effect.

Dispatch updateElement actions.

ImageToolOptions.tsx:

Visible when an image element is selected.

Controls for: Opacity, Blend Mode (dropdown), Filters (sliders/toggles for brightness, contrast, saturation, blur, grayscale, sepia), "Remove Background" button (if applicable to generic images, triggers AI flow), "Segment Anything" button (triggers AI flow).

Dispatch updateElement or AI flow actions.

DrawToolOptions.tsx (NEW):

Visible when activeTool === 'Draw'.

Controls for: Brush type selector (pen, pencil, airbrush, marker, etc.), Brush Size (slider), Brush Color (picker), Opacity (slider). Eraser tool options (size, hardness).

Dispatch updateToolSetting actions for the draw tool.

ElementCreationOptions.tsx:

Visible when activeTool === 'Elements'.

Buttons/icons to select sub-tool: Rectangle, Ellipse, Line, Polygon, Star.

Updates currentElementSubTool in useDesignStore.

TransformToolOptions.tsx (NEW - or integrated into each element's options):

Visible when any element is selected.

Precise numerical inputs for X, Y, Width, Height, Rotation.

Buttons for Flip Horizontal/Vertical.

Alignment buttons (align to canvas, align selected elements).

Dispatch updateElement or updateMultipleElements actions.

EffectsToolOptions.tsx (NEW):

Visible when an element supporting effects is selected.

Could be integrated into specific element options panels or be a separate panel.

UI for adding/managing effects like drop shadows, inner shadows, blurs (if not covered by basic filters).

VI. Layers Panel (src/components/design-studio/layers/LayersPanel.tsx) A dedicated UI component, possibly part of RightProperties or a separate toggleable sidebar.

Responsibilities:

Subscribes to useDesignStore for the elements array and selectedElementIds.

Renders a list of all elements, showing their type/name, a thumbnail (optional), visibility toggle, lock toggle.

Allows drag-and-drop reordering of layers (dispatches actions to reorder elements array or update zIndex).

Allows selecting elements by clicking on layer items (updates selectedElementIds in store).

Buttons for "Group", "Ungroup", "Delete Selected".

VII. History Controls (src/components/design-studio/history/UndoRedoControls.tsx) Typically part of the TopBar.tsx.

Responsibilities:

Subscribes to useDesignStore for history.past.length and history.future.length to enable/disable buttons.

"Undo" button: calls useDesignStore.undo().

"Redo" button: calls useDesignStore.redo().

VIII. Utility Libraries (src/lib/design-studio/) Contains pure functions and utilities supporting the Design Studio.

elementFactory.ts: Functions like createTextElement(config), createShapeElement(type, config) that return new element objects with default and provided properties, including unique IDs.

transformations.ts: Functions for calculating new bounding boxes after rotation, scaling points, etc. Used by store actions or interaction handlers.

historyManager.ts: If undo/redo logic is complex, it might be encapsulated here, providing functions for takeSnapshot, undoState, redoState that the Zustand store actions would call.

canvasDrawingUtils.ts: Advanced 2D canvas functions for rendering elements (especially complex shapes, text with effects, drawn paths) accurately for the "Download Design" feature. Handles rotation, scaling, and applying styles to a raw canvas context.

snapUtils.ts: Functions to calculate snapping positions when dragging or resizing elements, based on grid settings or proximity to other elements.

geometryUtils.ts: Helper functions for geometric calculations (e.g., point in polygon, line intersection, bounding box calculations).

This detailed structure aims for high modularity, clear separation of concerns, and robust state management, paving the way for implementing the full suite of advanced design editing features requested for ARTTOO. Each new tool or major feature within the Design Studio would likely involve creating new components within these directories and updating the designStore and relevant interaction handlers.

// src/stores/designStore.ts import { create } from 'zustand'; import { type TextElement, type ShapeElement, type ImageElement, type ProcessedImageElement, // Potentially: type DrawnPathElement, type GroupElement } from '@/types/design-elements'; // Assuming all element types are here

// Define a union type for all possible design elements type DesignElement = TextElement | ShapeElement | ImageElement | ProcessedImageElement; // Potentially add DrawnPathElement, GroupElement in the future: // type DesignElement = TextElement | ShapeElement | ImageElement | ProcessedImageElement | DrawnPathElement | GroupElement;

// Interface for the history state (for undo/redo) interface HistoryState { past: DesignState[]; present: DesignState; // The current state of the design future: DesignState[]; }

// Interface for the serializable parts of the design state that go into history interface DesignState { elements: DesignElement[]; selectedElementIds: string[]; activeTool: string; currentElementSubTool: string | null; toolSettings: { drawBrushType: string; drawBrushSize: number; drawBrushColor: string; drawOpacity: number; defaultFontFamily: string; defaultFontSize: number; defaultFontColor: string; // Future: Add other tool-specific settings as needed }; canvasZoom: number; canvasPan: { x: number; y: number }; gridSettings: { visible: boolean; size: number; snapToGrid: boolean; }; baseImage: string | null; // Note: canvasWidth, canvasHeight might be managed by the canvas component itself // or stored here if they need to be part of the undo/redo history. }

// Interface for the complete Zustand store, including actions interface DesignStore extends DesignState { history: HistoryState;

// --- Actions ---

// Element Actions addElement: (element: DesignElement) => void; removeElements: (elementIds: string[]) => void; updateElement: (elementId: string, updates: Partial<DesignElement>) => void; updateMultipleElements: (updates: Array<{ id: string; props: Partial<DesignElement> }>) => void; setSelectedElementIds: (ids: string[]) => void; clearSelection: () => void; bringToFront: (elementIds: string[]) => void; sendToBack: (elementIds: string[]) => void; duplicateElements: (elementIds: string[]) => void; // Future: groupElements: (elementIds: string[]) => void; // Future: ungroupElement: (groupId: string) => void;

// Tool Actions setActiveTool: (tool: string, subTool?: string | null) => void; updateToolSetting: (toolKey: keyof DesignState['toolSettings'], value: any) => void; // More specific typing can be added later

// Canvas Actions setCanvasZoom: (zoom: number) => void; setCanvasPan: (pan: { x: number; y: number }) => void; setGridVisibility: (visible: boolean) => void; setGridSize: (size: number) => void; setSnapToGrid: (snap: boolean) => void; setBaseImage: (imageUri: string | null) => void; clearCanvas: () => void;

// History Actions undo: () => void; redo: () => void; takeSnapshot: () => void; // Internal action to save current state to history }

// Function to get the initial state for the 'present' part of history // This ensures that 'present' is always a valid DesignState object const getInitialPresentState = (): DesignState => ({ elements: [], selectedElementIds: [], activeTool: 'Select', currentElementSubTool: null, toolSettings: { drawBrushType: 'pen', drawBrushSize: 5, drawBrushColor: '#000000', // Default black drawOpacity: 1, defaultFontFamily: 'system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif', defaultFontSize: 16, defaultFontColor: '#000000', // Default black }, canvasZoom: 1, canvasPan: { x: 0, y: 0 }, gridSettings: { visible: false, size: 20, snapToGrid: false, }, baseImage: null, });

export const useDesignStore = create<DesignStore>((set, get) => ({ // --- Initial State --- ...getInitialPresentState(), // Spread initial values for the main state history: { past: [], present: getInitialPresentState(), // Initialize present state for history future: [], },

// --- Action Implementations ---

// Element Actions addElement: (element) => { set((state) => { const newElements = [...state.elements, element]; return { elements: newElements }; }); get().takeSnapshot(); // Take snapshot after adding an element }, removeElements: (elementIds) => { set((state) => ({ elements: state.elements.filter(el => !elementIds.includes(el.id)), selectedElementIds: state.selectedElementIds.filter(id => !elementIds.includes(id)), })); get().takeSnapshot(); }, updateElement: (elementId, updates) => { set((state) => ({ elements: state.elements.map(el => el.id === elementId ? { ...el, ...updates } : el ), })); // Note: takeSnapshot is often called by the UI action that triggers updateElement, // especially after a drag/resize operation completes, or a property change is finalized. // For continuous updates (like live typing or dragging), snapshot might be debounced or taken at the end. }, updateMultipleElements: (updates) => { set((state) => ({ elements: state.elements.map(el => { const foundUpdate = updates.find(u => u.id === el.id); return foundUpdate ? { ...el, ...foundUpdate.props } : el; }), })); get().takeSnapshot(); }, setSelectedElementIds: (ids) => { set({ selectedElementIds: ids }); // No snapshot needed for just selection change typically }, clearSelection: () => { set({ selectedElementIds: [] }); }, bringToFront: (elementIds) => { set((state) => { const selectedElements = state.elements.filter(el => elementIds.includes(el.id)); const otherElements = state.elements.filter(el => !elementIds.includes(el.id)); return { elements: [...otherElements, ...selectedElements] }; }); get().takeSnapshot(); }, sendToBack: (elementIds) => { set((state) => { const selectedElements = state.elements.filter(el => elementIds.includes(el.id)); const otherElements = state.elements.filter(el => !elementIds.includes(el.id)); return { elements: [...selectedElements, ...otherElements] }; }); get().takeSnapshot(); }, duplicateElements: (elementIds) => { const { elements } = get(); const newElements: DesignElement[] = []; elementIds.forEach(id => { const original = elements.find(el => el.id === id); if (original) { const duplicate = { ...original, id: Date.now().toString() + Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 7), // More robust ID x: (original.x || 0) + 10, // Ensure x and y are numbers y: (original.y || 0) + 10, }; newElements.push(duplicate); } }); if (newElements.length > 0) { set(state => ({ elements: [...state.elements, ...newElements], selectedElementIds: newElements.map(el => el.id), // Select the new duplicates })); get().takeSnapshot(); } },

// Tool Actions setActiveTool: (tool, subTool = null) => { set({ activeTool: tool, currentElementSubTool: subTool, selectedElementIds: [] }); }, updateToolSetting: (toolKey, value) => { set((state) => ({ toolSettings: { ...state.toolSettings, [toolKey]: value, }, })); // No snapshot for tool setting changes usually, unless it directly creates an element },

// Canvas Actions setCanvasZoom: (zoom) => { set({ canvasZoom: Math.max(0.1, Math.min(zoom, 10)) }); // Example zoom limits }, setCanvasPan: (pan) => { set({ canvasPan: pan }); }, setGridVisibility: (visible) => { set(state => ({ gridSettings: { ...state.gridSettings, visible } })); }, setGridSize: (size) => { set(state => ({ gridSettings: { ...state.gridSettings, size: Math.max(5, size) } })); }, setSnapToGrid: (snap) => { set(state => ({ gridSettings: { ...state.gridSettings, snapToGrid: snap } })); }, setBaseImage: (imageUri) => { set({ baseImage: imageUri, elements: [], selectedElementIds: [] }); // Clear elements when base image changes get().takeSnapshot(); }, clearCanvas: () => { set({ elements: [], selectedElementIds: [], baseImage: null, // Potentially reset zoom/pan here too, or leave them // canvasZoom: 1, // canvasPan: { x: 0, y: 0 }, }); get().takeSnapshot(); },

// History Actions takeSnapshot: () => { set(state => { const { history, ...currentStateProperties } = state; // Create a serializable snapshot of the current design state const snapshot: DesignState = { elements: currentStateProperties.elements, // Ensure deep copy if elements are mutable beyond properties selectedElementIds: currentStateProperties.selectedElementIds, activeTool: currentStateProperties.activeTool, currentElementSubTool: currentStateProperties.currentElementSubTool, toolSettings: currentStateProperties.toolSettings, // Ensure deep copy canvasZoom: currentStateProperties.canvasZoom, canvasPan: currentStateProperties.canvasPan, gridSettings: currentStateProperties.gridSettings, // Ensure deep copy baseImage: currentStateProperties.baseImage, };

  // Avoid duplicate snapshots if state hasn't changed
  if (JSON.stringify(snapshot) === JSON.stringify(history.present)) {
    return {}; // No change in state, no new snapshot
  }
  
  const newPast = [...history.past, history.present];
  // Limit history size if needed
  // const MAX_HISTORY = 50;
  // if (newPast.length > MAX_HISTORY) {
  //   newPast.shift(); 
  // }

  return {
    history: {
      past: newPast,
      present: snapshot,
      future: [], // Clear future on new action
    },
  };
});
}, undo: () => { set(state => { const { past, present, future } = state.history; if (past.length === 0) return {}; // Nothing to undo

  const previousState = past[past.length - 1];
  const newPast = past.slice(0, past.length - 1);

  return {
    ...previousState, // Apply the previous state properties to the root store
    history: {
      past: newPast,
      present: previousState,
      future: [present, ...future],
    },
  };
});
}, redo: () => { set(state => { const { past, present, future } = state.history; if (future.length === 0) return {}; // Nothing to redo

  const nextState = future[0];
  const newFuture = future.slice(1);

  return {
    ...nextState, // Apply the next state properties to the root store
    history: {
      past: [...past, present],
      present: nextState,
      future: newFuture,
    },
  };
});
}, }));

// src/app/design-studio/page.tsx 'use client'; import * as React from 'react'; import { useState, useRef, useCallback, useMemo, useEffect } from 'react'; // Note: next/image import is removed as DesignCanvas or its children will handle image rendering import { UploadCloud, Scissors, Loader2, Download, Baseline, MousePointerSquareDashed, LayoutDashboard, Shapes as ShapesIcon, PenLine, Layers as LayersIcon, Sparkles as SparklesIcon, SlidersHorizontal as SlidersHorizontalIcon, History as HistoryIcon, Trash2, HardDriveUpload, ArrowUpFromLine, ArrowDownToLine, Copy, Square as SquareIcon, Circle as CircleIcon, } from 'lucide-react';

import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'; import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle } from '@/components/ui/card'; import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input'; import { Textarea } from '@/components/ui/textarea'; import { Label } from '@/components/ui/label'; import { useToast } from '@/hooks/use-toast'; import { removeBackground } from '@/ai/flows/remove-background';

import { LeftNav } from '@/components/layout/left-nav'; import { TopBar } from '@/components/layout/top-bar'; import { VerticalToolbar, designStudioToolbarItems as defaultToolbarItems } from '@/components/layout/vertical-toolbar'; import { RightProperties, type AccordionPanelItem } from '@/components/layout/right-properties'; import { SidebarProvider, SidebarInset } from '@/components/ui/sidebar'; import { DesignCanvas, type DesignCanvasProps } from '@/components/design-studio/canvas/DesignCanvas'; // Assuming DesignCanvasProps might be needed for type casting or reference import { type TextElement, type ProcessedImageElement, // This will likely be treated as an ImageElement with a flag type ImageElement, type ShapeElement, type DesignElement as StoreDesignElement, // Alias for clarity } from '@/types/design-elements'; import { useDesignStore } from '@/stores/designStore'; // Import the Zustand store

// Helper function to generate unique IDs (can be moved to a utils file later) const generateId = () => Date.now().toString(36) + Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 9);

export default function DesignStudioPage() { // --- Zustand Store Integration --- const store = useDesignStore(); // Get the whole store instance for actions

// Select states from the store const { elements, selectedElementIds, activeTool, currentElementSubTool, baseImage, toolSettings, // history, // For enabling/disabling undo/redo buttons } = useDesignStore(state => ({ elements: state.elements, selectedElementIds: state.selectedElementIds, activeTool: state.activeTool, currentElementSubTool: state.currentElementSubTool, baseImage: state.baseImage, toolSettings: state.toolSettings, // history: state.history, // Uncomment if undo/redo buttons are in this component }));

// --- Local UI State (primarily for async operations or complex interactions before committing to store) --- const [isProcessingAIRemoveBackground, setIsProcessingAIRemoveBackground] = useState(false);

// Dragging and Resizing states - these manage the interactive part of the operation. // The final result of these operations will be committed to the Zustand store. const [isDragging, setIsDragging] = useState(false); const [draggingElementId, setDraggingElementId] = useState<string | null>(null); const [dragStartOffset, setDragStartOffset] = useState<{ x: number; y: number }>({ x: 0, y: 0 }); // Temp state for element being dragged to allow smooth UI updates before committing to store const [tempDraggedElementProps, setTempDraggedElementProps] = useState<Partial<StoreDesignElement> | null>(null);

const [isResizing, setIsResizing] = useState(false); const [resizingElementId, setResizingElementId] = useState<string | null>(null); const [resizeStartPoint, setResizeStartPoint] = useState<{ x: number; y: number } | null>(null); const [resizeStartDimensions, setResizeStartDimensions] = useState<{ width: number; height: number; naturalWidth?: number; naturalHeight?: number; x: number; y: number; } | null>(null); // Temp state for element being resized const [tempResizedElementProps, setTempResizedElementProps] = useState<Partial<StoreDesignElement> | null>(null);

const fileInputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null); const canvasContainerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null); const { toast } = useToast();

// Effect to clear canvas on mount - uses store action useEffect(() => { console.log("DesignStudioPage: useEffect for blank canvas running on mount."); store.clearCanvas(); if (fileInputRef.current) { fileInputRef.current.value = ''; } }, [store]); // store is stable

const handleToolSelect = useCallback((toolLabel: string) => { let subTool: string | null = null; if (toolLabel === 'Elements') { subTool = store.currentElementSubTool || 'rectangle'; // Keep current or default } store.setActiveTool(toolLabel, subTool);

if (toolLabel === 'Uploads' && fileInputRef.current) {
  fileInputRef.current.onchange = (e) => handleElementImageUpload(e, 'generic');
  fileInputRef.current.click();
} else if (fileInputRef.current) {
  fileInputRef.current.onchange = handleBaseImageUpload;
}
}, [store]);

const handleBaseImageUpload = useCallback((event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => { const file = event.target.files?.[0]; if (file) { if (file.size > 5 * 1024 * 1024) { toast({ variant: "destructive", title: "File Too Large", description: "Max 5MB." }); if (event.target) event.target.value = ''; return; } const reader = new FileReader(); reader.onloadend = () => { store.setBaseImage(reader.result as string); toast({ title: "Base Image Uploaded" }); }; reader.readAsDataURL(file); } if (event.target) event.target.value = ''; }, [store, toast]);

const handleElementImageUpload = useCallback((event: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>, imageType: 'generic' | 'processedOverlay') => { const file = event.target.files?.[0]; if (file && canvasContainerRef.current) { if (file.size > 5 * 1024 * 1024) { toast({ variant: "destructive", title: "File Too Large", description: "Max 5MB." }); if (event.target) event.target.value = ''; return; } const reader = new FileReader(); reader.onloadend = () => { const newImg = new window.Image(); newImg.onload = () => { const canvasRect = canvasContainerRef.current!.getBoundingClientRect(); const MAX_DIM = imageType === 'processedOverlay' ? Math.min(canvasRect.width * 0.8, canvasRect.height * 0.8) : 200; let w = newImg.naturalWidth; let h = newImg.naturalHeight; const aspectRatio = w / h;

      if (w > MAX_DIM || h > MAX_DIM) {
        if (aspectRatio >= 1) { w = MAX_DIM; h = MAX_DIM / aspectRatio; }
        else { h = MAX_DIM; w = MAX_DIM * aspectRatio; }
      }

      const newImageElement: ImageElement = {
        id: generateId(), type: 'image', src: newImg.src,
        x: (canvasRect.width - w) / 2, y: (canvasRect.height - h) / 2,
        width: w, height: h,
        naturalWidth: newImg.naturalWidth, naturalHeight: newImg.naturalHeight,
        rotation: 0, opacity: 1,
        isProcessedOverlay: imageType === 'processedOverlay', // Flag for processed images
      };
      store.addElement(newImageElement as StoreDesignElement);
      store.setSelectedElementIds([newImageElement.id]);
      store.setActiveTool('Select');
      toast({ title: imageType === 'processedOverlay' ? "Processed Image Added" : "Image Element Added" });
    };
    newImg.src = reader.result as string;
  };
  reader.readAsDataURL(file);
}
if (event.target) event.target.value = '';
}, [store, toast]);

const handleRemoveBackground = useCallback(async () => { if (!baseImage) { toast({ variant: "destructive", title: "No Base Image" }); return; } setIsProcessingAIRemoveBackground(true); store.clearSelection(); try { const result = await removeBackground({ imageDataUri: baseImage }); if (result.processedImageDataUri && canvasContainerRef.current) { // Simulate file upload for the processed image to reuse logic const blob = await (await fetch(result.processedImageDataUri)).blob(); const processedFile = new File([blob], "processed_image.png", { type: blob.type }); const mockEvent = { target: { files: [processedFile] } } as unknown as React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>; handleElementImageUpload(mockEvent, 'processedOverlay'); } else { throw new Error("AI did not return a processed image."); } } catch (error) { console.error("Error removing background:", error); toast({ variant: "destructive", title: "Processing Failed", description: String(error) }); } finally { setIsProcessingAIRemoveBackground(false); } }, [baseImage, store, toast, handleElementImageUpload]);

const handleDownloadDesign = useCallback(() => { if (elements.length === 0 && !baseImage) { toast({ variant: "destructive", title: "Nothing to Download" }); return; } console.log("Download initiated. Elements:", elements, "Base Image:", baseImage); toast({ title: "Download (Placeholder)", description: "Actual download logic needs full implementation." }); // Actual canvas drawing logic for download will be complex and use store.elements }, [elements, baseImage, toast]);

const handleCanvasClick = useCallback((event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => { if (event.target !== canvasContainerRef.current || !canvasContainerRef.current) return; const rect = canvasContainerRef.current.getBoundingClientRect(); const x = event.clientX - rect.left; const y = event.clientY - rect.top;

if (activeTool === 'Text') {
  const newTextElement: TextElement = {
    id: generateId(), type: 'text', content: 'Your Text Here',
    x, y, fontSize: toolSettings.defaultFontSize,
    fontFamily: toolSettings.defaultFontFamily, color: toolSettings.defaultFontColor,
    rotation: 0, opacity: 1,
  };
  store.addElement(newTextElement as StoreDesignElement);
  store.setSelectedElementIds([newTextElement.id]);
  store.setActiveTool('Select');
} else if (activeTool === 'Elements') {
  const shapeType = store.currentElementSubTool === 'ellipse' ? 'ellipse' : 'rectangle';
  const newShapeElement: ShapeElement = {
    id: generateId(), type: shapeType,
    x: x - (shapeType === 'ellipse' ? 37.5 : 50), // Centering offset
    y: y - (shapeType === 'ellipse' ? 37.5 : 25),  // Centering offset
    width: shapeType === 'ellipse' ? 75 : 100,
    height: shapeType === 'ellipse' ? 75 : 50,
    fillColor: `hsl(${getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--primary-hsl')?.trim() || '257 57% 50%'} / 0.7)`,
    rotation: 0, opacity: 1,
    strokeColor: getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--foreground').trim() || '#000000',
    strokeWidth: 1,
    cornerRadius: shapeType === 'rectangle' ? 0 : undefined,
  };
  store.addElement(newShapeElement as StoreDesignElement);
  store.setSelectedElementIds([newShapeElement.id]);
  store.setActiveTool('Select');
} else if (activeTool === 'Select') {
  store.clearSelection();
}
}, [activeTool, store, toolSettings]);

// --- Element Interaction Handlers (Simplified for store integration) --- const getElementFromStore = useCallback((id: string) => elements.find(el => el.id === id), [elements]);

const handleElementMouseDown = useCallback((elementId: string, event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => { if (activeTool === 'Select' && canvasContainerRef.current) { event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation(); store.setSelectedElementIds([elementId]); const element = getElementFromStore(elementId); if (element) { setIsDragging(true); setDraggingElementId(elementId); const canvasRect = canvasContainerRef.current.getBoundingClientRect(); const mouseXInCanvas = event.clientX - canvasRect.left; const mouseYInCanvas = event.clientY - canvasRect.top; setDragStartOffset({ x: mouseXInCanvas - element.x, y: mouseYInCanvas - element.y }); setTempDraggedElementProps({ x: element.x, y: element.y }); // Init temp state document.body.style.cursor = 'grabbing'; } } }, [activeTool, store, getElementFromStore]);

const handleResizeHandleMouseDown = useCallback((elementId: string, event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => { if (activeTool === 'Select' && canvasContainerRef.current) { event.preventDefault(); event.stopPropagation(); const element = getElementFromStore(elementId); if (element) { setIsResizing(true); setResizingElementId(elementId); setResizeStartPoint({ x: event.clientX, y: event.clientY }); setResizeStartDimensions({ width: element.width, height: element.height, naturalWidth: (element as ImageElement).naturalWidth || element.width, naturalHeight: (element as ImageElement).naturalHeight || element.height, x: element.x, y: element.y, // Store initial position for complex resize logic if needed }); setTempResizedElementProps({ width: element.width, height: element.height }); // Init temp state setIsDragging(false); document.body.style.cursor = 'nwse-resize'; } } }, [activeTool, store, getElementFromStore]);

useEffect(() => { const handleGlobalMouseMove = (event: MouseEvent) => { if (!canvasContainerRef.current) return; const canvasRect = canvasContainerRef.current.getBoundingClientRect();

  if (isDragging && draggingElementId && tempDraggedElementProps) {
    const originalElement = getElementFromStore(draggingElementId);
    if (!originalElement) return;
    let newX = event.clientX - canvasRect.left - dragStartOffset.x;
    let newY = event.clientY - canvasRect.top - dragStartOffset.y;
    newX = Math.max(0, Math.min(newX, canvasRect.width - originalElement.width));
    newY = Math.max(0, Math.min(newY, canvasRect.height - originalElement.height));
    setTempDraggedElementProps({ x: newX, y: newY }); // Update temp state for smooth UI
  } else if (isResizing && resizingElementId && resizeStartPoint && resizeStartDimensions && tempResizedElementProps) {
    const originalElement = getElementFromStore(resizingElementId);
    if (!originalElement) return;

    const deltaX = event.clientX - resizeStartPoint.x;
    let newWidth = resizeStartDimensions.width + deltaX;
    let newHeight = resizeStartDimensions.height;

    if (originalElement.type === 'image' || (originalElement as ImageElement).isProcessedOverlay) {
      const aspectRatio = resizeStartDimensions.naturalWidth! / resizeStartDimensions.naturalHeight!;
      newWidth = Math.max(20, newWidth);
      newHeight = newWidth / aspectRatio;
      if (newHeight < 20) { newHeight = 20; newWidth = newHeight * aspectRatio; }
    } else if (originalElement.type === 'rectangle' || originalElement.type === 'ellipse') {
      const deltaY = event.clientY - resizeStartPoint.y;
      newHeight = resizeStartDimensions.height + deltaY;
      newWidth = Math.max(10, newWidth); newHeight = Math.max(10, newHeight);
    }
    setTempResizedElementProps({ width: newWidth, height: newHeight }); // Update temp state
  }
};

const handleGlobalMouseUp = () => {
  if (isDragging && draggingElementId && tempDraggedElementProps) {
    if (tempDraggedElementProps.x !== undefined && tempDraggedElementProps.y !== undefined) {
      store.updateElement(draggingElementId, { x: tempDraggedElementProps.x, y: tempDraggedElementProps.y });
      store.takeSnapshot(); // Snapshot after drag completes
    }
  } else if (isResizing && resizingElementId && tempResizedElementProps) {
     if (tempResizedElementProps.width !== undefined && tempResizedElementProps.height !== undefined) {
        store.updateElement(resizingElementId, { width: tempResizedElementProps.width, height: tempResizedElementProps.height });
        store.takeSnapshot(); // Snapshot after resize completes
    }
  }
  setIsDragging(false); setDraggingElementId(null); setTempDraggedElementProps(null);
  setIsResizing(false); setResizingElementId(null); setResizeStartPoint(null); setResizeStartDimensions(null); setTempResizedElementProps(null);
  document.body.style.cursor = 'default';
};

if (isDragging || isResizing) {
  window.addEventListener('mousemove', handleGlobalMouseMove);
  window.addEventListener('mouseup', handleGlobalMouseUp);
}
return () => {
  window.removeEventListener('mousemove', handleGlobalMouseMove);
  window.removeEventListener('mouseup', handleGlobalMouseUp);
  if (document.body.style.cursor !== 'default') document.body.style.cursor = 'default';
};
}, [ isDragging, draggingElementId, dragStartOffset, tempDraggedElementProps, isResizing, resizingElementId, resizeStartPoint, resizeStartDimensions, tempResizedElementProps, store, getElementFromStore // store is stable, getElementFromStore depends on elements ]);

useEffect(() => { if (fileInputRef.current) { if (activeTool === 'Uploads') { fileInputRef.current.onchange = (e) => handleElementImageUpload(e, 'generic'); } else { fileInputRef.current.onchange = handleBaseImageUpload; } } }, [activeTool, handleElementImageUpload, handleBaseImageUpload]);

// --- RightProperties Panel Logic (Simplified to use store) --- const rightPropertiesItems = useMemo((): AccordionPanelItem[] => { const items: AccordionPanelItem[] = []; const selectedId = selectedElementIds.length > 0 ? selectedElementIds[0] : null; const selectedElement = selectedId ? elements.find(el => el.id === selectedId) : null;

if (activeTool === 'Elements') {
  items.push({
    value: "create-element-options", title: "Create Element", icon: ShapesIcon,
    content: (
      <div className="space-y-2">
        <Label className="text-xs font-medium">Shape Type</Label>
        <Button variant={currentElementSubTool === 'rectangle' ? 'secondary' : 'outline'} size="sm" className="w-full justify-start" onClick={() => store.setActiveTool('Elements', 'rectangle')}>
          <SquareIcon className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> Rectangle
        </Button>
        <Button variant={currentElementSubTool === 'ellipse' ? 'secondary' : 'outline'} size="sm" className="w-full justify-start" onClick={() => store.setActiveTool('Elements', 'ellipse')}>
          <CircleIcon className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> Ellipse
        </Button>
      </div>
    )
  });
}

if (selectedElement && activeTool === 'Select') {
  const commonActions = [
    <div key="layer-ops" className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2 mt-2">
      <Button variant="outline" size="sm" onClick={() => store.sendToBack([selectedElement.id])}><ArrowDownToLine className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> To Back</Button>

    </div>,
    <Button key="dup" variant="outline" size="sm" className="w-full mt-2" onClick={() => store.duplicateElements([selectedElement.id])}>
      <Copy className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> Duplicate
    </Button>,
    <Button key="del" variant="outline" size="sm" className="w-full mt-2 border-destructive text-destructive hover:bg-destructive/10 hover:text-destructive" onClick={() => store.removeElements([selectedElement.id])}>
      <Trash2 className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" /> Delete
    </Button>
  ];

  const transformControls = [
    <div key="pos" className="mt-1">
        <Label className="text-xs font-medium">Position</Label>
        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2 mt-1">
            <Input type="number" value={selectedElement.x.toFixed(0)} onChange={e => store.updateElement(selectedElement.id, { x: parseInt(e.target.value) || 0 })} onBlur={() => store.takeSnapshot()} prefix="X:" className="h-8 text-xs" />
            <Input type="number" value={selectedElement.y.toFixed(0)} onChange={e => store.updateElement(selectedElement.id, { y: parseInt(e.target.value) || 0 })} onBlur={() => store.takeSnapshot()} prefix="Y:" className="h-8 text-xs" />
        </div>
    </div>,
    <div key="size" className="mt-2">
        <Label className="text-xs font-medium">Size</Label>
        <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2 mt-1">
            <Input type="number" value={selectedElement.width.toFixed(0)} onChange={e => store.updateElement(selectedElement.id, { width: Math.max(1, parseInt(e.target.value) || 1) })}  onBlur={() => store.takeSnapshot()} prefix="W:" className="h-8 text-xs" />
            <Input type="number" value={selectedElement.height.toFixed(0)} onChange={e => store.updateElement(selectedElement.id, { height: Math.max(1, parseInt(e.target.value) || 1) })} onBlur={() => store.takeSnapshot()} prefix="H:" className="h-8 text-xs" />
        </div>

    <div key="rot" className="mt-2">
        <Label htmlFor={`${selectedElement.id}-rotation`} className="text-xs font-medium">Rotation (°)</Label>
        <Input id={`${selectedElement.id}-rotation`} type="number" value={selectedElement.rotation} onChange={e => store.updateElement(selectedElement.id, { rotation: parseInt(e.target.value) || 0 })} onBlur={() => store.takeSnapshot()} className="text-sm mt-1 h-9" step="1" />

  if (selectedElement.type === 'text') {

          <div><Label className="text-xs font-medium">Font</Label>
            <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-2 mt-1">

    let newY = event.clientY - canvasRect.top - dragStartOffset.y;

    newY = Math.max(0, Math.min(newY, canvasRect.height - originalElement.height));
    setTempDraggedElementProps({ x: newX, y: newY }); // Update temp state for smooth UI
  } else if (isResizing && resizingElementId && resizeStartPoint && resizeStartDimensions && tempResizedElementProps) {
    const originalElement = getElementFromStore(resizingElementId);
    if (!originalElement) return;

    const deltaX = event.clientX - resizeStartPoint.x;
    let newWidth = resizeStartDimensions.width + deltaX;
    let newHeight = resizeStartDimensions.height;

    if (originalElement.type === 'image' || (originalElement as ImageElement).isProcessedOverlay) {
      const aspectRatio = resizeStartDimensions.naturalWidth! / resizeStartDimensions.naturalHeight!;
      newWidth = Math.max(20, newWidth);
      newHeight = newWidth / aspectRatio;
      if (newHeight < 20) { newHeight = 20; newWidth = newHeight * aspectRatio; }
    } else if (originalElement.type === 'rectangle' || originalElement.type === 'ellipse') {
      const deltaY = event.clientY - resizeStartPoint.y;
      newHeight = resizeStartDimensions.height + deltaY;
      newWidth = Math.max(10, newWidth); newHeight = Math.max(10, newHeight);

    setTempResizedElementProps({ width: newWidth, height: newHeight }); // Update temp state
  }

const handleGlobalMouseUp = () => {
  if (isDragging && draggingElementId && tempDraggedElementProps) {
    if (tempDraggedElementProps.x !== undefined && tempDraggedElementProps.y !== undefined) {
      store.updateElement(draggingElementId, { x: tempDraggedElementProps.x, y: tempDraggedElementProps.y });

    }
  } else if (isResizing && resizingElementId && tempResizedElementProps) {
     if (tempResizedElementProps.width !== undefined && tempResizedElementProps.height !== undefined) {
        store.updateElement(resizingElementId, { width: tempResizedElementProps.width, height: tempResizedElementProps.height });
        store.takeSnapshot(); // Snapshot after resize completes
    }
  }
  setIsDragging(false); setDraggingElementId(null); setTempDraggedElementProps(null);
  setIsResizing(false); setResizingElementId(null); setResizeStartPoint(null); setResizeStartDimensions(null); setTempResizedElementProps(null);
  document.body.style.cursor = 'default';
};

if (isDragging || isResizing) {
  window.addEventListener('mousemove', handleGlobalMouseMove);
  window.addEventListener('mouseup', handleGlobalMouseUp);
}
return () => {
  window.removeEventListener('mousemove', handleGlobalMouseMove);
  window.removeEventListener('mouseup', handleGlobalMouseUp);
  if (document.body.style.cursor !== 'default') document.body.style.cursor = 'default';
};
}, [ isDragging, draggingElementId, dragStartOffset, tempDraggedElementProps, isResizing, resizingElementId, resizeStartPoint, resizeStartDimensions, tempResizedElementProps, store, getElementFromStore // store is stable, getElementFromStore depends on elements ]);

useEffect(() => { if (fileInputRef.current) { if (activeTool === 'Uploads') { fileInputRef.current.onchange = (e) => handleElementImageUpload(e, 'generic'); } else { fileInputRef.current.onchange = handleBaseImageUpload; } } }, [activeTool, handleElementImageUpload, handleBaseImageUpload]);

if (selectedElement && activeTool === 'Select') {
  const commonActions = [

Gemini
Okay, Cap'n! The "Maximum update depth exceeded" error is a tricky one. It usually means there's an unintentional loop where a component update triggers another update, and so on, until React gives up. The error stack pointing to Button in VerticalToolbar is a key clue.

One common cause for such issues in Zustand (or Redux, Context) is when a component re-renders too frequently due to its selector returning new object references even if the underlying data hasn't meaningfully changed for that component. This can sometimes trigger effects or prop changes in children that lead to a loop.

The selector in DesignStudioPage currently is: useDesignStore(state => ({ elements: state.elements, selectedElementIds: ..., ... })) This function creates and returns a new object on every run. If any part of the entire Zustand state changes, this selector runs, returns a new object, and DesignStudioPage re-renders, even if the specific properties it cares about (elements, activeTool, etc.) are deeply the same.

We can optimize this by using a shallow equality check for the selector. Zustand provides shallow for this.

Plan:

Import shallow from zustand/shallow in src/app/design-studio/page.tsx.
Update the useDesignStore hook in DesignStudioPage to use shallow as the equality function: useDesignStore(state => ({ ... }), shallow)
This will ensure that DesignStudioPage only re-renders if the actual values of elements, selectedElementIds, activeTool, etc., change, not just if their containing object reference from the selector is new. This can often break unintended update loops.

Here are the changes:

    }
  } else if (isResizing && resizingElementId && tempResizedElementProps) {
     if (tempResizedElementProps.width !== undefined && tempResizedElementProps.height !== undefined) {
        store.updateElement(resizingElementId, { width: tempResizedElementProps.width, height: tempResizedElementProps.height });
        store.takeSnapshot();
    }

};

Gemini
Ahoy, Cap'n! This "Maximum update depth exceeded" error, with the trail leading to store.clearCanvas() within a useEffect in DesignStudioPage, is a classic case of a runaway effect.

Here's what's likely happening:

The useEffect in DesignStudioPage is set up to run when the store object (from useDesignStore()) changes:
useEffect(() => {
  store.clearCanvas();
  // ...
}, [store]);
The store object itself, as returned by useDesignStore(), is generally a stable reference. However, the effect calls store.clearCanvas().
store.clearCanvas() internally calls set({...}) to update the store's state (clearing elements, baseImage, etc.) and then get().takeSnapshot() which also modifies the store's history.
This state modification might be perceived by React or Zustand in a way that causes the DesignStudioPage component to re-render.
Upon re-render, the useEffect runs again because it's part of a new render cycle, even if the store reference itself hasn't changed.
This leads to store.clearCanvas() being called repeatedly, causing an infinite loop of state updates and re-renders.
The intention of this useEffect is likely to clear the canvas once when the page mounts. To achieve this, the dependency array of the useEffect should be empty ([]).

I'll modify src/app/design-studio/page.tsx to change the dependency array of that specific useEffect from [store] to [].

Here's the change:

9bf34e0b

Restore
This change ensures that the useEffect responsible for clearing the canvas only runs once when the DesignStudioPage mounts, which should break the infinite update loop.

Morgan

Okay, Cap'n! After reviewing the current state and the overall goals for ARTTOO, the next most logical and impactful step is to significantly enhance the realism of the static "Image Try-On" feature by implementing an AI-powered realistic tattoo application.

Current Situation:

The "Image Try-On" page allows users to upload a body photo and a tattoo design.
It can segment the skin on the body photo (remove background).
It overlays the tattoo design, allowing for manual adjustments (position, scale, rotation, opacity, blend mode).
However, the tattoo overlay is still a flat 2D image placed on top of another. It doesn't conform to skin texture, lighting, or subtle body contours.
Chosen Next Step: AI-Powered Realistic Tattoo Application Flow

Reasoning:

Directly Addresses "Digital Try-On" Realism: This is a core tenet of ARTTOO. Moving beyond a simple overlay to an AI-composited image where the tattoo appears to interact with the skin's lighting, shadows, and texture will be a major user experience improvement. It's a step towards the "body-contour-warping" aspiration.
Leverages Existing AI Infrastructure (Genkit): We have a robust setup for creating and using Genkit AI flows. This new feature fits perfectly within that model.
Builds on Previous Work: It uses the outputs of existing features (segmented body photo, tattoo design with removed background).
High User Impact: A more realistic preview, even on a static image, will be far more convincing and useful for users planning a tattoo.
Feasible Iteration: While perfect realism is a high bar, even a noticeable improvement in how the tattoo blends with the skin will be valuable. We can iterate on the AI prompt and capabilities over time.
Implementation Plan:

Create a New AI Flow (src/ai/flows/apply-tattoo-realistically.ts):

Purpose: To take a body part image and a tattoo design (with a transparent background) and generate an image where the tattoo appears realistically applied to the skin, considering lighting, texture, and basic contours.
Input Schema (ApplyTattooRealisticallyInput):
bodyPhotoDataUri: string (The photo of the body part. This could be the original or, ideally, the skin-segmented version for better results).
tattooDesignDataUri: string (The tattoo design image, must have a transparent background).
tattooPlacementDescription: string (A textual description of where and how the tattoo should be placed, e.g., "Place this tattoo on the center of the forearm, wrapping slightly around the curve. Ensure the top of the tattoo is oriented towards the elbow.") This will help guide the AI if simple coordinate-based placement isn't directly part of this AI step.
intensityHint: string (Optional, e.g., "Make it look like a fresh, dark tattoo" or "Make it look like a slightly faded, settled tattoo").
Output Schema (ApplyTattooRealisticallyOutput):
compositedImageDataUri: string (The new image with the tattoo applied).
feedbackMessage: string (Optional feedback from the AI about the process).
Prompt Engineering: The prompt will instruct the AI to:
Identify the main body surface in bodyPhotoDataUri.
Overlay the tattooDesignDataUri according to the tattooPlacementDescription.
Crucially, blend the tattoo with the skin. This means adjusting the tattoo's appearance to match the lighting, shadows, and apparent texture of the skin.
Attempt to subtly warp or distort the tattoo to follow simple visible contours on the body part.
Consider the intensityHint.
Genkit Model: Use googleai/gemini-2.0-flash-exp as it supports image input and output.
Safety Settings: Apply appropriate safety settings, similar to other image generation/manipulation flows.
Update src/ai/dev.ts:

Import the new apply-tattoo-realistically.ts flow.
Integrate into src/app/try-on/page.tsx (Front-end Changes - for a later step, but good to outline):

New UI Element: Add a button like "Realistically Apply with AI" or "AI Finalize Placement".
Workflow:
User uploads body photo and tattoo, performs initial manual placement/scaling/rotation.
User potentially runs skin segmentation.
User clicks "Realistically Apply with AI".
The front-end would need to capture the current state:
The bodyImageForCanvas (segmented or original).
The tattooImage (after ensuring its background is transparent, possibly by calling the removeBackground flow if it hasn't been already).
Challenge: Convert the current on-canvas tattooPosition, tattooScale, tattooRotation into a meaningful tattooPlacementDescription for the AI. This might be tricky.
Simpler MVP for placement: The AI flow might initially just try to place it centrally or based on a very generic instruction, and the user might need to re-do fine-tuned placement on the AI-composited image using the existing controls if the AI's initial placement isn't perfect. Or, the AI-generated image completely replaces the body image and the separate tattoo layer.
Call the applyTattooRealistically flow.
On success, update the bodyImageForCanvas with the compositedImageDataUri. The separate draggable tattoo element might then be hidden or removed, as the tattoo is now part of the main image.
A Textarea could be added for users to provide or refine the tattooPlacementDescription or intensityHint.
Let's start by creating the AI flow apply-tattoo-realistically.ts and adding it to dev.ts. The front-end integration will be a subsequent step.

Okay, Cap'n! After evaluating our current position and the ARTTOO feature roadmap, the next most logical and impactful step is to enhance the visual representation in the Avatar Studio by transitioning from basic styled divs to using SVG elements.

Reasoning:

Advances "Parametric MVP" for Avatar Studio: The current div-based avatar is very rudimentary. Moving to SVG allows for more defined shapes, better layering, and more nuanced control via parameters, which is key for a "parametric" system.
Improves User Experience: An SVG avatar, even if simple, will look more like an actual character than styled rectangles. This makes the customization process more engaging and the purpose of the controls clearer.
Better Foundation for Future Enhancements: SVGs provide a good stepping stone. The logic for mapping parameters to SVG attributes can later be adapted if we move to more complex rendering like 2D Canvas animations or even WebGL.
Direct Visual Feedback: Users will see more distinct changes in the avatar's form (e.g., head shape, torso, basic clothing shapes) as they adjust parameters, rather than just color and overall dimension changes of a single block.
Utilizes Web Standards: SVG is a well-supported web standard, requiring no external libraries for basic rendering.
Implementation Plan:

We will modify the central avatar display area in src/app/avatar-studio/page.tsx to render an <svg> element. Inside this SVG, we'll define basic shapes (like <ellipse> for head, <rect> for torso/limbs, <path> for simple clothing or hair) whose attributes (fill, stroke, dimensions, path data) will be dynamically controlled by the existing state variables.

Main SVG Canvas: Replace the main div rendering the avatar with an <svg> tag. Set a viewBox for scalable graphics.
Body Parts:
Head: An <ellipse> or <circle>. Its fill will be skinTone.
Torso: A <rect>. Its fill will be skinTone, dimensions influenced by avatarHeight and avatarWidth.
(Optional for this step) Limbs: Simple <rect> elements for arms and legs, fill by skinTone.
Hair:
A <path> or a group of simple shapes.
fill based on a predefined hair color (we can add a hair color state later).
The shape/visibility could be influenced by hairStyle and hairLength. For MVP, hairStyle might select one of a few predefined paths, and hairLength could scale its vertical dimension. If "bald", it's not rendered.
Clothing:
Shirt: A <path> or <rect> layered over the torso.
fill will be shirtColor.
The shape could be one of a few predefined paths based on shirtType.
Parameter Mapping:
avatarHeight: Could scale the main SVG group vertically or specifically adjust heights of torso/legs.
avatarWidth: Could scale the main SVG group horizontally or adjust widths of torso/shoulders.
This will be an iterative process. We'll start with the basic structure and get the head, torso, and a simple shirt shape reacting to skinTone, shirtColor, avatarHeight, and avatarWidth. Hair and more distinct clothing styles will be more complex and can be refined further.

Gemini
Okay, Cap'n! After our recent fixes and feature additions, the next most logical step is to enhance the "Download Result" functionality on the "Image Try-On" page (src/app/try-on/page.tsx).

Currently, when a user has a manual tattoo overlay active (i.e., AI realism has not been applied), the download uses html2canvas to capture the viewing area. While functional, html2canvas can sometimes be slow and may not perfectly replicate complex CSS effects like blend modes, and it forces a white background.

We can significantly improve this by using a client-side <canvas> element to directly composite the body image and the tattoo overlay. This method offers better performance, more accurate rendering of blend modes and opacity, and allows us to maintain transparency if the original images have it.

Reasoning:

Improved Download Quality: Direct canvas compositing provides a more faithful reproduction of the visual setup, especially for blend modes and opacity, compared to html2canvas.
Better Performance: Rendering directly to a 2D canvas for image composition is generally faster than html2canvas trying to interpret and redraw the DOM.
Preserves Transparency: This method allows us to create a final PNG with a transparent background if the source images (body and tattoo) support it.
Refines a Core Feature: Downloading the result is a key user action, and improving its quality enhances the overall utility of the "Image Try-On" tool.
Implementation Plan:

We will modify the handleDownloadResult function in src/app/try-on/page.tsx. The logic for downloading an AI-blended result (where showSeparateTattooOverlay is false) will remain the same. The change will be in the branch that handles manual overlays (where showSeparateTattooOverlay is true and canvasContainerRef.current exists).

New logic for manual overlay download in handleDownloadResult:

Check for Necessary Elements: Ensure canvasContainerRef.current, bodyImageForCanvas, and tattooImageForOverlay are available.
Get Container Dimensions: From canvasContainerRef.current.clientWidth and clientHeight. These will be the dimensions of our output image.
Load Images:
Create Image objects for bodyImageForCanvas (bodyImgEl) and tattooImageForOverlay (tattooImgEl).
Use Promise.all to wait for both images to load. This is crucial to get their naturalWidth and naturalHeight.
Setup Offscreen Canvas:
Create an offscreen canvas: const offscreenCanvas = document.createElement('canvas');
Set its dimensions: offscreenCanvas.width = containerWidth; offscreenCanvas.height = containerHeight;
Get the 2D context: const ctx = offscreenCanvas.getContext('2d'); If ctx is null, handle the error.
Draw Body Image:
Replicate the object-contain behavior: Calculate the scale and offsets needed to draw bodyImgEl centered and fitted within the offscreenCanvas.
ctx.drawImage(bodyImgEl, offsetX, offsetY, scaledBodyWidth, scaledBodyHeight);
Draw Tattoo Overlay:
ctx.save();
Calculate the display dimensions of the tattoo based on its natural size and tattooScale: const tattooDisplayWidth = tattooImgEl.naturalWidth * tattooScale; const tattooDisplayHeight = tattooImgEl.naturalHeight * tattooScale;
Apply transformations to the context. The tattooPosition is relative to the top-left of the canvasContainerRef.
Translate to the tattoo's center: ctx.translate(tattooPosition.x + tattooDisplayWidth / 2, tattooPosition.y + tattooDisplayHeight / 2);
Rotate: ctx.rotate(tattooRotation * Math.PI / 180);
Set opacity: ctx.globalAlpha = tattooOpacity;
Set blend mode: ctx.globalCompositeOperation = tattooBlendMode as GlobalCompositeOperation; (The BlendMode enum values should match standard canvas composite operations).
Draw the tattoo image centered around the new origin: ctx.drawImage(tattooImgEl, -tattooDisplayWidth / 2, -tattooDisplayHeight / 2, tattooDisplayWidth, tattooDisplayHeight);
ctx.restore();
Generate Data URL:
const dataUrlToDownload = offscreenCanvas.toDataURL('image/png');
Trigger Download:
Use the existing link creation and click simulation logic to download the dataUrlToDownload.
Loading State: The existing isDownloading state will continue to be used to provide user feedback.
This will replace the html2canvas call for the manual overlay scenario, leading to a higher quality and potentially faster download.

State Management for History:

Introduce two new state variables: history (an array of DesignElement[][] representing past states of the canvas elements) and historyIndex (an integer representing the current position in the history stack).
Initialize history with the initial elements state.
Initialize historyIndex to 0.
Updating Canvas Elements and History:

Create a new function, updateElementsAndRecordHistory(newElementsOrCallback: DesignElement[] | ((prevElements: DesignElement[]) => DesignElement[])).
This function will:
Determine the newActualElements based on whether newElementsOrCallback is a direct array or an updater function.
Update the elements state with newActualElements.
Slice the history array up to the current historyIndex + 1.
Add newActualElements to this sliced history.
Update the history state with this new array.
Update historyIndex to be the new last index of the history (newHistoryArray.length - 1).
Replace all direct calls to setElements (in addElement, updateElement, deleteSelectedElement, handleClearCanvas, and image upload) with calls to this new updateElementsAndRecordHistory function.

If historyIndex > 0:
Decrement historyIndex.
Set elements to history[historyIndex - 1].
Deselect any selected element (setSelectedElementId(null)).
Show a toast: "Undo applied".
Implement handleRedo function:

If historyIndex < history.length - 1:
Increment historyIndex.
Set elements to history[historyIndex + 1].
Deselect any selected element.
Show a toast: "Redo applied".
Integrate Undo/Redo into the UI:

Modify the designStudioToolbarItems array (which is passed to VerticalToolbar).
Add two new items:
Undo: Icon Undo2, action handleUndo. Its active prop (which VerticalToolbar uses for enabled/disabled state styling for Delete) should be historyIndex > 0.
Redo: Icon Redo2, action handleRedo. Its active prop should be historyIndex < history.length - 1.
The VerticalToolbar component's logic for handling the active prop for disabling will be used.
Initialization with localStorage:

When elements are loaded from localStorage during the initial useState for elements, also initialize history to [[...parsedElements]] and historyIndex to 0.
When handleClearCanvas is called, after clearing elements, also reset history to [[]] and historyIndex to 0.
This will add robust Undo/Redo capabilities to the Design Studio.

Morgan
Try fixing this error: Unhandled Runtime Error: Hydration failed because ...

Gemini
You've hit a classic hydration error, Cap'n! This often happens when content that depends on client-side information (like localStorage for the theme) is rendered differently by the server and the client during the initial page load.

The error message "Hydration failed because the server rendered HTML didn't match the client" and the diff showing Moon vs Sun icons point directly to the ThemeToggleButton rendering differently.

Here's the breakdown:

Server Render: The server doesn't have access to localStorage. Your ThemeProvider's useState initializer likely falls back to defaultTheme (e.g., 'dark'). So, the server renders the page with the 'dark' theme, and the ThemeToggleButton shows the Sun icon.
Client Initial Render/Hydration: When the client JavaScript loads, your ThemeProvider's useState initializer runs again. This time, typeof window !== 'undefined' is true, so it reads from localStorage. If the stored theme is 'light', the initial theme state on the client becomes 'light'.
Mismatch: React then tries to hydrate the server-rendered HTML. It sees the server sent a Sun icon, but because the client's initial theme state is 'light', the client wants to render a Moon icon. This mismatch causes the hydration error.
To fix this, we need to ensure that the server and the client render the exact same thing initially. Then, after the client has mounted and hydrated, we can update the theme based on localStorage.

Here's how we'll adjust src/context/theme-provider.tsx:

d0bfda93

Restore
This change ensures that useState initializes theme to defaultTheme for both server and the initial client render. Then, a useEffect hook (which only runs on the client after hydration) reads from localStorage and updates the theme. This will fix the hydration mismatch. You might see a quick flash of the default theme before the user's preferred theme loads, but the application will no longer error.

Gemini
You're right, Cap'n, that "Invalid URL" error is a classic sign that the src prop for the next/image component received a string that wasn't a valid URL or data URI. Given the context of how localStorage handles null values by converting them to the string "null", this is the most likely culprit for the bodyImage state.

When bodyImage becomes the string "null", it's truthy (so bodyImage && !isLoadingBodyImage passes), but "null" is not a valid image source, leading to the error.

To fix this, I'll adjust the loadStateFromLS and saveStateToLS helper functions within src/app/try-on/page.tsx. The goal is:

When saving a state that is null (like an image URI that's been cleared), we should remove the item from localStorage instead of storing the string "null".
When loading, if localStorage.getItem(key) returns null (meaning it's not set or was explicitly removed), we correctly fall back to the defaultValue.

saveStateToLS: When saving a value that is null (e.g., when an image is cleared), it will now call localStorage.removeItem(key) instead of storing the string "null". For non-null values, it continues to store them as strings (or JSON strings if isJson is true).
loadStateFromLS: It now expects that if localStorage.getItem(key) returns null, it means the item was either never set or was explicitly set to null (and thus removed by the updated saveStateToLS). Gemini
You're right, Cap'n, that "Invalid URL" error clearly indicates that bodyImage is being passed the string "null" instead of the actual JavaScript null value or a valid data URI. This happens when localStorage.getItem retrieves a key that was previously stored with the string value "null".

My previous fix for loadStateFromLS was on the right track but didn't fully cover the scenario where a non-JSON string value stored in localStorage is literally the string "null".

The current loadStateFromLS in src/app/try-on/page.tsx has this logic:

    // ...
    if (item === null) { // Item not found or was explicitly removed
        return defaultValue;
    }
    // If item is found, it's a stored string. Parse if JSON, otherwise return as is.
    return isJson ? JSON.parse(item) : (item as unknown as T);
    // ...
If item is the string "null" and isJson is false (which is the case for our image URIs), the (item as unknown as T) part will return the string "null".

We need to explicitly check for this case when isJson is false.

Builds on Existing State: We can achieve this by reordering the elements array, as the rendering order in ArtooStudioCanvas is directly tied to the array order (last element in the array is rendered on top).
Implementation Plan:

I'll modify src/app/design-studio/page.tsx primarily:

Update rightPropertiesItems for "Layers" Panel:

For each layer item displayed in the "Layers" accordion panel:
Add "Move Up" and "Move Down" buttons (e.g., using ArrowUpCircle and ArrowDownCircle or similar icons from lucide-react).
These buttons will call new handler functions: handleMoveElementUp(elementId) and handleMoveElementDown(elementId).
The "Move Up" button should be disabled if the element is already at the top of the stack (last in the elements array).
The "Move Down" button should be disabled if the element is already at the bottom of the stack (first in the elements array).
Implement Handler Functions in CanvasArea:

handleMoveElementUp = (elementId: string) => { ... }:
Find the index of the element with elementId in the elements array.
If the element exists and is not already the last element (topmost), create a new array where this element is swapped with the element at index + 1.
Call updateElementsAndRecordHistory with this new elements array.
Display a toast: "Layer moved up."
handleMoveElementDown = (elementId: string) => { ... }:
Find the index of the element with elementId in the elements array.
If the element exists and is not already the first element (bottommost), create a new array where this element is swapped with the element at index - 1.
Call updateElementsAndRecordHistory with this new elements array.
Display a toast: "Layer moved down."
Ensure Canvas Re-renders Correctly:

Since the ArtooStudioCanvas iterates through the elements array for rendering, changing the order in the elements state and triggering a re-render will automatically update the visual stacking order on the canvas.
This will provide users with essential control over the arrangement of their design elements.

Builds on Existing Concepts: We can leverage the concept of an activeTool, canvas interaction, and modifying the elements array.

isErasing: boolean (to track if the mouse is currently down with the eraser tool).

Eraser Interaction Logic (src/app/design-studio/page.tsx - in CanvasArea):

handleCanvasMouseDown:
If activeTool === 'eraser':
Set isErasing = true.
Call a new function performErasure(event.clientX, event.clientY) to check and delete elements at the initial click point.
Prevent default to avoid selecting other elements.
handleCanvasMouseMove:
If activeTool === 'eraser' and isErasing:
Call performErasure(event.clientX, event.clientY) to continuously check and delete elements as the user drags.
handleCanvasMouseUp:
If activeTool === 'eraser' and isErasing:
Set isErasing = false.
The updateElementsAndRecordHistory should have been called within performErasure if elements were deleted.
performErasure(mouseX: number, mouseY: number) function:
Get the artboard's bounding rectangle (artboardRef.current.getBoundingClientRect()).
Calculate the mouse position relative to the artboard.
Define the eraser's circular area: center at (relativeMouseX, relativeMouseY) with radius currentEraserSize / 2.
Iterate through a copy of the elements array (to avoid issues if modifying it directly during iteration).
For each element:
If element.type === 'drawing':
Intersection Check: Determine if the eraser's circular area intersects with the DrawingElement's bounding box. A simple check:
Element's rect: elX, elY, elWidth, elHeight.
Eraser circle: eraserCenterX, eraserCenterY, eraserRadius.
Check if elX < eraserCenterX + eraserRadius && elX + elWidth > eraserCenterX - eraserRadius && elY < eraserCenterY + eraserRadius && elY + elHeight > eraserCenterY - eraserRadius. This is a basic Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) intersection with the eraser's bounding box. A more precise circle-to-rectangle intersection can be implemented later if needed.
If they intersect, add the element.id to a list of IDs to delete for this pass.
If any elements are marked for deletion:
Filter them out from the main elements state.
Call updateElementsAndRecordHistory with the new elements array.
Maybe show a subtle toast or visual feedback if many elements are erased quickly.
Visual Eraser Cursor (src/components/design-studio/canvas/ArtooStudioCanvas.tsx):

Props: Pass activeTool and currentEraserSize to the canvas.
Rendering:
If activeTool === 'eraser', render a temporary SVG circle that follows the mouse cursor over the artboard. This circle's diameter should be currentEraserSize, and it should have a visible stroke (e.g., a dashed outline or a semi-transparent fill) to indicate the eraser area. This is purely visual feedback.
The artboardCursor should be updated to something like 'none' or a custom eraser cursor if the visual SVG eraser is prominent enough.
This approach introduces a destructive eraser for drawings. It doesn't do partial path erasure (which is much more complex) but provides a functional way to remove drawn elements by "painting" over them.

That "Cannot access 'X' before initialization" error in React, especially with hooks like useEffect and useCallback, almost always points to an issue where a function or variable is used in a hook's dependency array or closure before its definition has been fully processed in the component's render cycle.

Gemini
Okay, Cap'n! We've laid the groundwork for the "Curved Line Tool" by allowing users to define a series of points and marking the resulting DrawingElement with brushType: BrushType.SmoothCurve. However, as we noted, it currently renders these paths as straight line segments.

The next most logical step is to implement the actual smooth curve rendering for these DrawingElements and for the live preview of the Curve tool. This will make the tool visually functional and deliver on its name.

For this, we'll use SVG's built-in capabilities for smooth quadratic Bézier curves (Q and T path commands). This provides a good balance of smoothness and ease of implementation for paths defined by a sequence of user-clicked points.

Implementation Plan:

Modify src/components/design-studio/canvas/ArtooStudioCanvas.tsx:
New Helper Function getSmoothCurvePathD:
This function will take an array of PathPoint[] (relative points for a completed DrawingElement, or absolute points for the live preview).
It will return an SVG path string (d attribute) that renders a smooth curve through these points.
Logic for getSmoothCurvePathD:
If points.length < 2, return a simple path (e.g., "M x y" for 1 point, or "M x1 y1 L x2 y2" for 2 points).
If points.length === 2, it's a straight line: return \M ${points[0].x},${points[0].y} L ${points[1].x},${points[1].y}`;`
If points.length > 2:
Start path: let d = \M ${points[0].x},${points[0].y}`;`
First curve segment (quadratic Bézier from points[0] to points[2] using points[1] as the control point): d += \ Q ${points[1].x},${points[1].y} ${points[2].x},${points[2].y}`;`
For subsequent points (i from 3 up to points.length - 1):
Use the smooth quadratic Bézier T command: d += \ T ${points[i].x},${points[i].y}`;`
The T command automatically calculates the control point to make a smooth continuation from the previous quadratic curve.
Return d.
Rendering Completed DrawingElements:
In the loop that renders elements:
When element.type === 'drawing':
If (element as DrawingElement).brushType === BrushType.SmoothCurve:
Call const pathData = getSmoothCurvePathD((element as DrawingElement).points);
Use this pathData for the d attribute of the SVG <path>.
Else (for Pen, Pencil, Line, Polyline), keep the current straight-segment path generation: const pathData = drawingEl.points.map((p, i) => \${i === 0 ? 'M' : 'L'} ${p.x} ${p.y}`).join(' ');`
Rendering Live Preview for Curve Tool:
When activeTool === 'curved-line' and isDrawingPolyline && currentPolylinePoints.length > 0:
To render the already placed segments of the curve being drawn:
const liveCurvePathData = getSmoothCurvePathD(currentPolylinePoints);
Use this liveCurvePathData in the SVG <path> for the preview of committed segments.
The "rubber-band" line (from the last point in currentPolylinePoints to previewPolylineNextPoint) should remain a straight line, as it represents the next potential segment before it's committed to the curve.
This approach provides a visually smooth curve that passes through the start point (P0), the second-to-last intermediate point (P(n-1) if Pn is the last point), and the end point (Pn), while using other intermediate points to define the curvature. It's a good starting point for smooth curve drawing.

Let's get these curves smoothed out!
